subject: Architecture
title: The Millennium Bridge: London's Wobble
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Millennium Bridge: London's Wobble.

hook.text: London's Millennium Bridge opened in June 2000 — and closed two days later because it swayed dangerously.

buildup.text: The sleek, low-profile suspension footbridge was designed by Norman Foster and sculptor Anthony Caro.

discovery.text: When pedestrians walked, their footsteps synchronized with the bridge's sway — amplifying the wobble.

twist.text: This 'synchronous lateral excitation' had never been studied — it wasn't in any engineering textbook.

climax.text: Engineers installed 91 dampers to absorb the motion. The bridge reopened in 2002 and hasn't wobbled since.

punchline.text: People walk in sync. Nobody knew that could break a bridge.

quiz.question: What caused the Millennium Bridge to wobble?
options: Wind forces on the bridge's flat profile
Pedestrians' footsteps synchronized with the bridge's sway
Tidal forces from the River Thames pushed the foundations

details.summary: London's Millennium Bridge began swaying alarmingly on its opening day in June 2000 when thousands of pedestrians crossed simultaneously. The lateral vibrations — caused by synchronized footsteps — forced a two-year closure and a £5 million retrofit with dampers to control the wobble.
details.whyItMatters: The Millennium Bridge revealed that engineers had underestimated how pedestrians synchronize their steps in response to lateral motion — a feedback loop that no bridge code had accounted for, leading to global changes in pedestrian bridge design.
takeaways: The Millennium Bridge wobbled on opening day due to synchronized footsteps
Lateral vibrations forced a two-year closure for damper installation
It changed global understanding of pedestrian-induced bridge vibration

faq.question: Why did the Millennium Bridge wobble?
faq.answer: Pedestrians on a swaying bridge instinctively adjust their gait to match the motion, which amplifies it. This synchronous lateral excitation created a positive feedback loop: the more the bridge swayed, the more people walked in sync, which made it sway more.

faq.question: How was the problem fixed?
faq.answer: Engineers installed 37 viscous dampers and 52 tuned mass dampers beneath the deck to absorb lateral energy. The £5 million fix completely eliminated the wobble, and the bridge — designed by Foster + Partners and Arup — has functioned perfectly since reopening in 2002.
